findings.title: CAPTCHA answer leaked by /rest/captcha enables unauthenticated form submission bypass
findings.analysis: The endpoint http://lab-mutator:3000/rest/captcha (GET, no authentication) returns the server-computed answer to the math captcha in plaintext: {"captchaId":N,"captcha":"EXPR","answer":"VAL"}. This endpoint feeds the contact/feedback form, whose POST (http://lab-mutator:3000/api/Feedbacks/) requires a correct captcha answer. Verified across 5 fresh captcha generations that the answer is server-computed and unique per request (1*6*6→36; 10*3-4→26; 9+6*3→27; 3-2+4→5; 10*3-4→26) and that captchaIds increment (2,3,4,5,6). Differential test with a single fresh request pair: POST /api/Feedbacks/ with the leaked answer → HTTP 201 success (feedback id=10); with an arbitrary wrong answer → HTTP 401 "Wrong answer to CAPTCHA. Please try again." The frontend code only consumes .captcha and .captchaId and deliberately ignores .answer, so this is a server-side anti-automation flaw, not a client-side prediction. Post without any captcha fields yields HTTP 500 "WHERE parameter captchaId has invalid undefined value", so the answer leak is the viable bypass route. Severity: Broken Anti Automation (confirms the target's own "CAPTCHA Bypass" challenge, id=14).
findings.false_positive_check: The .answer field is never used by the client, is server-generated, and changes per request with an incrementing captchaId, so it cannot be a stale/cached client-side value. The 401/201 differential with the exact same captchaId proves the server validates the answer against the leaked value.

repro_requests.note: HTTP 201 with leaked answer; HTTP 401 with any other value

findings.title: Unauthenticated /rest/memories exposes all user accounts including password hashes and deluxe tokens
findings.analysis: GET http://lab-mutator:3000/rest/memories (no authentication) returns HTTP 200 with every user's full record embedded in each memory. Records include id, username, email, password (32-hex hash), role, deluxeToken, lastLoginIp, totpSecret, isActive, createdAt/updatedAt. Five unique users observed: admin (bkimminich, bjoern.kimminich@gmail.com), deluxe (bjoern@owasp.org), and three customer/deluxe web3-enabled accounts. Password values are 32-hex strings (consistent with MD5), and deluxe membership tokens are exposed alongside. Severity: Sensitive Data Exposure. The same app correctly returns 401 on other endpoints without auth (/rest/wallet/balance, /rest/user/authentication-details/, /rest/basket/), confirming the auth enforcement works and /rest/memories is specifically unguarded.
findings.false_positive_check: Other REST endpoints in the identical app gate properly (401 without credentials), proving /rest/memories is an anomalous unauthenticated leak rather than expected app behavior. The exposed fields include secret-bearing values (password hashes, deluxe tokens) that are never part of a public user profile.

findings.title: Account existence enumerable via /rest/user/security-question endpoint
findings.analysis: GET http://lab-mutator:3000/rest/user/security-question?email=X returns HTTP 200 for existing emails with {"question":{"id":N,"question":"...","createdAt":...}} and HTTP 200 {} for non-existing emails. Combined with the user-email exposure from BHB-002, this lets an actor confirm which emails are registered and obtain their security-question IDs/text, enabling targeted password-recovery abuse or phishing. Severity: Information disclosure / Account enumeration.
findings.false_positive_check: Both cases are HTTP 200 but the body structure differs deterministically (question object vs empty object), tested against a known existing email and two distinct nonexistent emails returning {}.
